chapter: Honors, Gibson and Dorsey late years
title: Awards from the New Jersey Jazz Society and Portland's musicians' local
summary: Leeman describes his bronze plaque from the New Jersey Jazz Society, the fourth musician so honored, and another from his hometown local 364 in Portland.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: In remembering my thoughts last night, I remembered I have a plaque here, a bronze plaque, it's 20 by 30 inches, and it was given to me by the New Jersey Jazz Society, because I mentioned them yesterday and the wonderful things they did to continue the preservation of jazz.

Anyway, the plaque reads "New Jersey Jazz Society to Cliff Leeman, a musician among drummers, his playing has enriched the jazz heritage immensely, providing a standard by which others must be judged. The award is presented by

the New Jersey Jazz Society, February 12, 1978."
Up until that date, I was the fourth musician so honored. The others, I believe -- if I recall, were Vic Dickenson, Joe Venuti, Jess Stacey, Milt Gabler and John S. Wilson, eminent music critic of the New York Times, was on the nominating committee, and I am grateful to them.
To me, that's my Oscar. I started to say, also, this year Wild Bill Davison had been so honored, and he will be over here from Europe -- he lives in Denmark -- Copenhagen, and I will be in concert with him in a couple places, especially for nostalgia, back at Eddie Condon's club for a week, around June. And he's been so honored, and since I'm starting my day with an ego trip, I might as well describe another plaque received last year. That's hanging below the aforementioned Jersey Jazz bronze. This is another bronze plaque, and it reads "To Cliff Leeman, the world's greatest drummer par excellence, from Local 364 AF of M, Portland, Maine, March 23, 1978."
They may have been a bit carried away with the inscription, as that's my hometown local, but nevertheless, it was presented to me in March in concert with the -- well, I was in concert at the auditorium in Portland, Maine, with the World's Greatest Jazz Band, but it was cancelled out because of snow.
